**Session summary: brain — phase-0 epic re-sync (#402, PR #403)**

## Goal
Phase-0 bookkeeping of epic #313, after a full-scope architecture audit of `main` @ `5ef85df`: re-sync the docs that drifted from the shipped tree, clear the standing drift-guard, and close tickets already satisfied in code. Ref: issue #402, PR #403.

## What was done
- **`docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md` re-synced.** It still claimed the reviewer flow-guarantees were inert (#317) and that the release gate ran after the tag (#210) — both shipped. Also corrected GitLab parity (all 8 MR gates blocking since Q5 Phase 5; the residual is rung-2/rung-3, #130) and replaced the "un-ticketed" M4 prose with the new ticket refs.
- **`AGENTS.md` regenerated** from its 5 SOURCE_DOCS via the antigravity backend — the M3 merge changed `reviewer-protocol.md`, leaving the drift-guard red. Suite 2263/2264 → 2264/2264.
- Epic #313 body updated with a dated status block; #369 and #263 closed as satisfied-in-code; M4 hard gate decomposed into #396-#401.

## BUG FOUND — the engram transport drops `issue`, and it blocks #368 / T2.1
While capturing this very record scoped to issue #402, the standing REQ-C4-1 contract test went red: the record failed round-trip id-equality. Root cause, traced through the seam:

- `buildRecord` includes `issue` in the hashInput (per memory-format.md:67), so a scoped record hashes differently.
- `importRecord` (record -> engram observation) has **no home for `issue`** — the observation shape is `{type, project, title, content, created_at, scope}`.
- `exportObservation` therefore cannot restore it, so the recomputed id differs from the stored id (`rec-4e5cce32ee0b4047` vs the stored `rec-c0d159bba82a6a95`).

Consequence: **any record carrying `issue` fails REQ-C4-1 today.** This is the mechanical reason #368 sits at 0% adoption — populating the field is not merely unadopted, it is currently *impossible* without breaking the round-trip contract. Since T2.1 memory-gate promotion depends on issue-scoped records, this seam is on the critical path for that promotion. The record was therefore written WITHOUT `issue`, matching every other record in the store, and the defect filed separately.

This is a seam-blindness defect of exactly the class M10 (#335) exists to close: green suite, contract silently unsatisfiable in the one direction nobody exercised.

## Findings worth carrying forward
- **The epic body drifted from its own tickets.** A roadmap pass derived from it proposed #210 as "1.1 first item" — #210 is closed and shipped. A source-of-truth doc needs a re-sync ritual or it misdirects the next agent.
- **M3 core is merged but the milestone exit is not met.** `5ef85df` wired the refuter (via `lib/causal-admission.mjs`) and tier-activated `/2`, but there are still no inline per-line comments — the literal exit criterion. Residuals: #381 (findings do not round-trip: render emits a YAML list, parse reads a JSON scalar), #382 (self-review fail-open in code, masked by config), `follow_ups[]` wired but unreachable, `/2` undogfoodable while brain declares `tier: lite`.
- **M4 was the biggest tracking gap**: the epic hard gate lived only as prose. Now #396 (rollback/atomic), #397 (clobber asymmetry), #398 (downgrade ratchet), #399 (corrupt-JSON lockout), #400 (npx brain init), #401 (danger-path e2e — makes the gate checkable).
- **Recurring defect class**: "one rule, two implementations" — #315, #316, #340. Worth batching as one initiative with drift-guards.

## Decisions
- One PR for both files: same atomic cause (the M3 merge), 130 lines, splitting would double the gate ritual for docs-only changes.
- Record written without `issue` rather than shipping a store that fails its own contract test.
- No `status:approved` applied by the agent — that is the human keystroke per #124 doctrine.

**Session summary: brain — M3 post-merge defect cleanup (#381, #382) + roadmap re-sync**

## Goal
Continue Phase 1 after the M3 core merge (`5ef85df`, #394): fix the two known reviewer defects, close the M3 residual tracking gap, and re-sync epic #313 so the roadmap is derivable from tickets rather than prose.

## What shipped
- **#381 → PR #406 (`c881a04`).** `findings` and `follow_ups` now survive the `renderVerdict` → `parseVerdict` round trip. Root cause: `renderVerdict` emits a YAML block list, `parseVerdict` read it with `scalar()`, whose `^findings:[ \t]*(.+)$` requires same-line content. Only `findings: []` matched. `follow_ups` was rendered by M3 but never parsed by anything — write-only since it shipped.
- **#382 → PR #407 (`e67dff8`).** Self-review abstention now fails closed at boot when `reviewer.handle` is empty. The same missing handle also made the anti-loop guard inert (it compares `lastVerdict.author` against that handle), so one fix restored two guards. The fail-open was deliberate, not an oversight — a strict guard would have abstained from every review while the handle was unresolvable — but that premise expired with #367.

## Tickets filed (M3 residuals — the milestone exit is NOT met)
- **#409** — `regulated`-tier e2e. Recommended FIRST: it is the harness the other two need to prove anything.
- **#405** — inline per-line `comments[]`, GitHub+GitLab parity. Needs an ADR-0020 amendment and a Tier-2 promotion of `vcs-contract.md` before any code: no contract for it exists yet.
- **#408** — no evaluator emits `pre-existing`/`base-only`; `follow_ups[]` is unreachable and the refuter never fires.
- **#404** — engram transport drops `issue`; blocks #368 → T2.1 promotion.
- **#410** — this memory materialization.

## Epic #313 re-synced
Critical path **inverted deliberately**: M4 (#396–#401) is now the highest-priority track, with M3 closure in parallel. Rationale recorded in the body: M4 is the hard gate blocking external adopters *today*; M3 residuals block reviewer *completeness*. The two touch disjoint surfaces, so nothing serialises them. Added a cross-cutting section for #404 (it belongs to no milestone yet blocks #368 → T2.1) and a standing rule for future agents: work described only in prose in that body is a bug — file an issue for it.

## Process notes that cost time
- Worktree-per-issue is the repo's workflow (`AGENTS.md`, load-bearing). `brain:ticket:start --worktree` fails in Claude-Code-on-the-web (`VCS token not found in .env` — the container has the GitHub MCP server, not a `gh` token); reproduce the branch convention manually from `deriveBranchType` + the 40-char slug rule.
- Worktrees do not inherit `node_modules`; symlink it or nothing runs.
- A combined branch being green does not prove each split half is green — run the full suite per worktree. Baseline on `e67dff8` is 2268 tests.
- Commit signing is impossible in this container (0-byte `commit_signing_key.pub`, no private key, no `ssh-keygen`); merged history already carries unsigned Claude commits.
- Deleting remote branches is blocked by the git proxy; `fix/issue-381-382-reviewer-roundtrip` is orphaned and needs deleting via the GitHub UI.

**Defect class: render/parse asymmetry hidden by testing only the empty encoding (brain, #381)**

`renderVerdict` serialised `findings` as a YAML block list; `parseVerdict` deserialised it with a scalar regex requiring content on the same line. Every non-empty findings list was silently dropped on the round trip.

**The generalisable lesson is why the full suite stayed green.** The only encoding that round-tripped — `findings: []` — was the only encoding under test. Coverage over a serializer/parser pair proves nothing unless the tests exercise the *non-degenerate* shape.

Two practices adopted in the fix, worth repeating for any wire-format work in this repo:
1. Tests drive the real `buildVerdict` → `renderVerdict` pair and parse the actual output. Hand-written fixture strings encode the author's belief about the format, which is exactly the thing under doubt.
2. New tests were run against the OLD parser to confirm they fail (3 of 4 did). The 4th — the empty case — passes against both and was kept deliberately, as an in-repo record of the blind spot that hid the defect.

Related: this is the same "green in test, inert in production" class that M10 (#335) exists to close. It was found by reading the code, not by a failing test, which is itself evidence for #409 — brain runs the `lite` tier, so the whole `/2` path has no production exercise.

**M3 shipped consumers without producers — three wired-but-unreachable paths (brain)**

After the M3 core merge, three code paths exist, are correct, and can never execute in production:

1. **`follow_ups[]`** — `verdict.mjs:51` routes a `causal_disposition` of `pre-existing`/`base-only` into it, `schema-v2.mjs` admits both values, `reviewer-protocol.md:216,222` documents them. **No evaluator emits either.** `causal-admission.mjs:23` states why, correctly: none of the current checks compare against base closely enough to claim it honestly, and "inventing the claim would be worse than omitting it". The gap is that no check which *can* make the claim was ever built. Tracked in #408.
2. **The refuter** (`evaluators/refuter.mjs`, #284) — runs only when a blocker carries `evidence_class: 'inferential'`. No evaluator produces inferential findings, so it is a documented no-op, deliberately wired so a future producer needs no second integration point. Same ticket, #408.
3. **The entire `/2` tier** — activation routes `lite`/`standard` → `/1` and `regulated` → `/2`, and brain declares `lite` (ADR-0026, #358). Everything M3 built is covered by unit tests and by nothing else. Tracked in #409.

**Consequence to carry forward:** #381 made `follow_ups` *readable*, not *populated* — it moved from broken to empty, not to working. Do not read a green suite or a merged PR as evidence that this feature works end to end.

**Empirical evidence for #404, found while inspecting the store:** zero records across `2026-06.jsonl`, `2026-07.jsonl` and `2026-08.jsonl` carry an `issue` field. That is the "~0% adoption" #368 describes, and the cause is the transport dropping the field, not authors omitting it. Note `computeRecordId` DOES hash `issue` when present, so the format supports it — only the transport does not.

**Session summary: brain — #396 slice 1, restore-point rollback for brain:upgrade**

## Goal
Pick up the brain 1.1 line and advance M4 — the epic #313 hard gate that blocks external
adopters from upgrading safely. Owner chose M4 over M3 closure, then chose to deliver #396
as a two-slice chain.

## Accomplished
- **#396 slice 1 shipped to review** — PR #412 (draft), chain `main ← feature/issue-396-rollback
  ← PR #412 ← PR#2`. `copyManaged` now snapshots every path it may write before the first
  write and restores those bytes on any throw; an incomplete rollback KEEPS its snapshot and
  reports where. Symlinked managed paths are refused up front. Suite 2268 → 2282.
- **Full SDD change dir written** at `openspec/changes/issue-396-upgrade-rollback/` —
  proposal, spec (REQ-396-1..9 with scenarios and negative controls), design, tasks, plus
  `brain-drafts/adr-0027-upgrade-rollback-is-restorable-not-atomic.md`.
- **Three follow-up issues filed**: #413, #414, #415. Epic #313 re-synced with a status block,
  a rewritten M4, and an explicit priority table for the next agent.

## Discoveries
1. **#396's stated exit criterion is unachievable as written.** `rename(2)` is atomic for ONE
   path; the managed payload spans four disjoint locations (`brain/**`, `.github/**`,
   `.gemini/**`, root files), so no single directory swap can commit it. Multi-file atomicity
   needs a journal. Restated as *restorability*, with each residual gap named — ADR-0027 draft,
   unsigned.
2. **A signal handler cannot interrupt a synchronous fs loop.** Measured: SIGINT at 40ms into a
   935ms sync copy loop → the loop ran to completion (i=60000) and the handler fired after;
   the same loop with a `setImmediate` yield aborted at i=2251. So registering a handler is not
   a mid-write abort — it suppresses the default terminate action, which is the only thing that
   genuinely half-applies a tree. The real managed write is 366 files in ~23ms.
3. **`spawnSync` returns `{status: null, signal}` when the child dies by signal.** A first
   revision claimed, as measured, that a Ctrl-C during `npm install` was caught by the deferred
   interrupt guard. It was not: `if (r.status !== 0)` fires first, reporting the interrupt as
   "install failed — check repo access" and collapsing exit 130 into 1. Registering the handler
   is what kept the parent alive to reach that branch, so the slice introduced that regression.
   Fixed by testing `r.signal` before `r.status`. Recorded rather than rewritten out of history.
4. **`existsSync` follows symlinks.** A dangling symlink at a managed path therefore read as
   absent, was recorded as created-by-this-run, and was DELETED on rollback — while
   `copyFileSync` wrote through the link to a target outside the repo, and the rollback reported
   success. The feature corrupting what it exists to protect. Presence must be judged with
   `lstat`.
5. **A `finally` is the wrong place to discard a restore point.** It runs after `catch`, so it
   deleted the snapshot on the incomplete-rollback path — the one branch where the snapshot is
   the only surviving copy of the consumer's bytes, and the same branch whose message tells the
   operator to go inspect them. Only a complete rollback may discard.
6. **Annotating a caught error can throw.** Modules are strict mode, so
   `err.rollbackIncomplete = …` raises a TypeError on a string, frozen Error or null — replacing
   the real failure AND dropping the dirty-tree signal, which made the CLI report a clean
   rollback over a dirty tree. `specialMerge` is caller-supplied on an exported API, so this
   needs no brain-side bug to reach.
7. **A test suite can be green and still miss the dominant shape.** The first test round always
   left exactly ONE entry in `toCopy` — the one that throws — so plain-copy rollback was never
   exercised, despite 364 of 366 real managed files being plain copies. Every rolled-back write
   in the suite came from a merge fn. Fixed by sorting the write order and adding REQ-S6-10.
8. **`brain:review` at `tier: lite` resolves to `brain-review/1`**, which has no
   findings-producing evaluator: `findings: []` means "nobody looked", not "the code is clean".
   `/2` — the half that wires causal-admission and the refuter — is `regulated`-only. This is
   epic #313's #409 observed live, not a defect.
9. **The reviewer identity is declared, never proven.** `identity.mjs` returns
   `reviewerConfig.handle` and nothing cross-checks the token against it, so the §10 self-review
   abstention and the anti-loop lock are forgeable. Filed as #413; sibling of #382.
10. **`actor-check`'s `lite` evidence is a distinct ACT, not a state.** The approved-label event
    must be strictly later than the PR's head commit, so every push invalidates the previous
    approval. Working as designed — Q5's fix for the stale-green class — but it will read as a
    broken CI to anyone who has not seen it.

## Corrections made to my own earlier claims
- Reported `TIER_PARAMS.lite.diffBudget` and `.artefacts` as unconsumed "one rule, two
  implementations" divergences. **Both were wrong**: `diffBudget` is read by `brain-check.mjs`,
  `brain-audit.mjs` and `merge-walk.mjs`; `artefacts` by `phase-order-check.mjs`. `check-refs`
  demanding all four artefacts is a deliberately tier-independent STRUCTURAL check. The wrong
  conclusion came from a mutilated grep (`rg -r` consumed the pattern as a replacement string).

## Next steps
- **#396 slice 2 — the on-disk journal.** The M4 hard gate stays CLOSED until it lands. It must
  INVERT `createRestorePoint`'s entry-time clearing of a pre-existing snapshot: once recovery
  exists, a leftover snapshot is evidence to replay, not debris. Flagged inline.
- Human: re-apply `status:approved` on #396 after the last push; ratify or reject ADR-0027;
  Tier-2 promotions for #397, #405 and #414.
- Then #397/#398/#399, #401, #413, and M3 closure (#409 → #405 → #408).

## Relevant files
- `brain/scripts/lib/installer.mjs` — `createRestorePoint`, `annotateRollback`, guarded write loop
- `brain/scripts/lib/installer.test.mjs` — REQ-S6-1..14
- `brain/scripts/brain-upgrade.mjs` — signal-before-status, rollback reporting, interrupt handling
- `docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md` — partial fix with all four residual gaps enumerated
- `openspec/changes/issue-396-upgrade-rollback/` — proposal, spec, design, tasks, ADR-0027 draft

**Session summary: brain — M4 upgrade safety (#396, #399, #398 closed; #397 designed and handed off)**

## Goal
Advance M4 — epic #313's HARD GATE, which blocks external adopters from upgrading
safely. Closed #396, #399 and #398; designed #397 and handed it off.

## Accomplished
- **#396 CLOSED** — restore point + on-disk journal + explicit `--recover` + an exclusive
  lock. ADR-0027 signed. Took EIGHT adversarial review rounds.
- **#399 CLOSED** — merge pre-flight + `--skip-merge <path>`; the corrupt-JSON lockout has
  an escape.
- **#398 CLOSED** — downgrade guard before the install, naming the config keys left ahead.
- **#397 DESIGNED, ratified, NOT implemented** — handed to a fresh agent.
- Spun off and closed by the maintainer: **#413** (reviewer identity now verified against
  the token) and **#418** (lite distinct-act re-arms only on FOREIGN commits — ADR-0026
  Amendment 1). Still open: **#414** (Tier-2), **#415** (cosmetic).

## Discoveries that cost the most to find
1. **A green suite proves nothing about a CLI it never runs.** Twice on #396 a fully green
   suite hid a broken product: once the feature did nothing (the `acquireLock` call site
   was deleted as collateral of a scripted edit), once `brain:upgrade` failed 100% of the
   time (the run read its own live lock as a competitor and refused itself). Both passed
   ~2290 tests. The fix was REQ-J-9 (the lock is HELD while it works) + REQ-J-10 (the
   upgrade completes and the bytes change). **Neither is sufficient alone.**
2. **A cleanup that judges locally will eventually delete something another site owns.**
   Four consecutive rounds produced that same shape, each introduced by the previous fix:
   a `finally` discarding the snapshot; a retry clearing the preserved copy; a catch
   destroying the evidence a refusal pointed at; `breakStaleLock` deleting a LIVE run's
   mutex. Resolved structurally with `inspectRestorePoint()` — ONE reader, ONE verdict
   (clean/debris/interrupted/corrupt/live-run) — and an ALLOW-list at the one remaining
   cleanup site.
3. **Signal handlers cannot interrupt a synchronous fs loop.** Measured: SIGINT at 40ms
   into a 935ms sync copy ran to completion, handler after. So registering a handler is
   not a mid-write abort — it stops the default action from killing the process, which is
   the only thing that half-applies a tree. Corollary, also measured: a run wedged on a
   hung managed path can then only be ended with SIGKILL.
4. **"Could not read it" is not "nobody owns it".** Widening lock reclaim to unowned locks
   accidentally widened it to UNREADABLE ones (EACCES/EIO/EMFILE/ESTALE), inverting the
   stated property from "it strands, it never permits" to permitting.
5. **schemaVersion has TWO writers with DIFFERENT meanings** — `ensureBrainConfig`
   (env:init) writes the newest MIGRATION version, `migrateConfig` writes the installed
   PACKAGE version, and migrations top out below the package. A downgrade guard trusting
   that field alone missed the six most recent of sixteen tags — the fresh-adopter
   population the gate exists for. Compare against the highest thing actually TRUE.
6. **AGENTS.md is GENERATED and its inputs straddle the ownership line.** `brain/HOME.md`
   matches neither `managed` nor `local`, so the consumer owns it. Plain-copying AGENTS.md
   therefore hands every consumer BRAIN's AGENTS.md, compiled from BRAIN's HOME.md — a file
   describing the wrong repository, in every consumer, from the first upgrade. This is the
   finding #397 does not contain and it reshaped the design.
7. **The collision check conflates two facts.** dest-vs-INCOMING answers "do these differ",
   not "did the consumer edit this". The missing third point is free: before the install,
   `node_modules/brain/<path>` is what brain shipped LAST time.

## Corrections I had to make to my own claims
- I wrote that #399 "strengthened" the #180 clobber guard. It WEAKENED it: I moved the
  assertion from the call site to the declaration, and mutating `specialMerge: mergeMap`
  to `{}` reproduced #180 with the whole suite green. Fixed with a behavioural test.
- I described reading the OUTGOING migration list as a tradeoff to apologise for. It is the
  only thing that works — a target's own list can never contain a migration above itself.
- Two "one rule, two implementations" divergences I reported (`diffBudget`, `artefacts`)
  were FALSE. Both params are consumed. The wrong conclusion came from `rg -rn`, where
  `-r` silently consumed the pattern as a replacement string.

## Method that worked, and should be kept
Measure the real behaviour before designing — three of the four M4 tickets had premises
that had already shifted. Write the test FIRST and prove it red. Drive the real CLI, not
the library API. Run one adversarial review per slice: the two I nearly skipped as "small
and safe" each found a real hole in the target population.

## Next steps
- **#397 implementation** — classification RATIFIED 04/08/2026, phases 2-4 unblocked,
  handed to a fresh agent. Tier-2 signature already obtained; do not re-litigate the table.
- **#401** — the danger-path e2e. **This is what makes the hard gate checkable**; three of
  its four paths now have real behaviour to assert, the fourth arrives with #397.
- **#400** — `npx brain init`, independent.
- **THE HARD GATE IS STILL CLOSED.** It opens when #401 is green, not when the fixes land.

## Relevant files
- brain/scripts/lib/installer.mjs — restore point, journal, recovery, lock, pre-flight, downgrade helpers
- brain/scripts/brain-upgrade.mjs — the CLI surface and every refusal path
- brain/scripts/lib/installer-journal.integration.test.mjs — REQ-J-*, REQ-M-*, REQ-D-* (all drive the real CLI)
- brain/project/decisions/adr-0027-upgrade-rollback-is-restorable-not-atomic.md
- openspec/changes/issue-397-clobber-asymmetry/ — the ratified design awaiting implementation
